candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, item 1 under CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS PERMIT
candidates.exact_span: Discharges from the facility may enter Lower Animas Ditch / Hampton Arroyo and/or Williams Arroyo in Water body Segment 20.6.4.98 / 99, with a critical low flow of 0 cfs. Discharges may also enter Water body Segment 20.6.4.404 or Segment 20.6.403 in the San Juan River Basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which receiving segments apply, whether discharge is to one or multiple water bodies, and the stated critical low flow (0 cfs) could change which water-quality-based numeric limits are selected and which monitoring or dilution assumptions govern compliance evaluation.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, item 1 under CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS PERMIT
candidates.exact_span: Previous permit identified the receiving water as a classified perennial stream, with a critical low flow (4Q3) for the Animas River, above Estes Arroyo as 184 cfs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting this prior-permit baseline versus the new receiving-water description could change whether limit revisions are treated as superseding old dilution or flow assumptions, affecting which numeric limits and monitoring contexts are considered operative for FY2025 comparisons.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, item 2 under CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS PERMIT
candidates.exact_span: Updated Minimum Quantification Level language in Part II of the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How MQL language is interpreted can determine whether reported measurements are quantified enough to be compared against enforceable numeric limits or must be treated as non-comparable or report-only for compliance purposes.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, item 3 under CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS PERMIT
candidates.exact_span: Biomonitoring test is changed from 48-hour Acute test to 7-day Chronic test based on updated critical dilution and updated receiving stream information.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the acute or chronic biomonitoring requirement applies, and how 'updated critical dilution and updated receiving stream information' is read, could change both the applicable toxicity limit/metric for Purpose A and the monitoring obligation type and frequency for Purpose B.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, item 4 under CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS PERMIT
candidates.exact_span: TRC limit is changed from 0.019 mg/L to 0.011 mg/L based on updated critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different interpretation of which TRC limit is in force, or how 'updated critical dilution' maps to the enforceable limit, would directly change whether reported TRC measurements are evaluated against 0.019 mg/L or 0.011 mg/L.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, item 5 under CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS PERMIT
candidates.exact_span: Quarterly monitoring and reporting requirements for Cyanide total recoverable have been established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting whether quarterly cyanide monitoring is newly required, and for which periods it is operative, could change whether monitoring was required during FY2025 and whether absent cyanide results indicate a missing-evidence case versus no applicable obligation.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, item 6 under CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS PERMIT
candidates.exact_span: Monitoring and reporting requirements for Delta-BHC study have been established in the draft permit based on delta-BHC effluent testing data submitted by the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Delta-BHC study monitoring is a standing obligation or conditioned on prior effluent testing could change monitoring-applicability determinations for Purpose B and how missing Delta-BHC results are classified for Purpose C.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, APPLICANT LOCATION and ACTIVITY
candidates.exact_span: This permitting action is for the discharge of backwash and flushing water originating from the potable water treatment plant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How broadly 'backwash and flushing water' is interpreted could change which outfalls, parameters, and discharge events are in scope for limit applicability, monitoring requirements, and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, APPLICANT LOCATION and ACTIVITY
candidates.exact_span: The Water Treatment Plant (WTP) consists of four plants, operated separately, at the same location.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the four plants are treated as separate discharge points or a single facility could change which measurements are paired with which limits and whether plant-specific monitoring obligations or missing-data cases must be evaluated separately.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, APPLICANT LOCATION and ACTIVITY
candidates.exact_span: Two of the four plants go through a flush cycle with raw water approximately every four to five hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting which plants discharge during flush cycles, and how often, could change whether discharge occurred during a monitoring period and thus whether monitoring or numeric limit comparisons were required versus documented no-discharge or not-required states.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, APPLICANT LOCATION and ACTIVITY
candidates.exact_span: Filter backwash using potable water occurs from once per day to once every three to four days depending on the plant and the time of year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Plant- and season-dependent backwash frequency could change whether discharge-triggered monitoring was required in specific FY2025 periods and how missing results should be classified when discharge may not have occurred.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, APPLICANT LOCATION and ACTIVITY
candidates.exact_span: Samples are collected prior to discharge at the entrance to the pipe leading to the open channel to the Lower Animas Ditch.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The specified sampling location determines which reported measurements are tied to the permitted discharge point for limit comparison and whether monitoring evidence at other points in the flow path is adequate or leaves applicability unresolved.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, APPLICANT LOCATION and ACTIVITY
candidates.exact_span: The backwash and system flush flows through the WTP’s sump system to an on-site settling pond (i.e., backwash pond) with an outlet to an open ditch, then through a driveway culvert, then through a pipe to an open channel to the Lower Animas Ditch.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How this flow path is read could affect which point is the relevant outfall for limit and monitoring applicability and whether interim locations create separate discharge or sampling obligations.

candidates.locator: page 4, section statement_of_basis, APPLICANT LOCATION and ACTIVITY
candidates.exact_span: The sediment stockpile is tested using Toxicity Characteristic
candidates.computation_change_reason: Even though the sentence is truncated in this segment, interpreting whether stockpile toxicity testing constitutes a monitoring requirement could change which non-effluent monitoring obligations are considered applicable during FY2025.
